definition_zh: 整洁的；井井有条的；简洁巧妙的；纯的（酒）；小巧匀称的
definition_en: tidy and in good order; simple and skilfully done; drunk without ice or water; small and well shaped
core_image: 桌面上书本按高矮排成一线，笔尖都朝同一个方向
scene: 宿舍的桌上，书本按高矮排成一线，几支笔都朝同一个方向摆着。His desk stayed neat even during the exam week.
sceneCN: 这里是「整洁的」（第 1 个义项：摆放有序、不凌乱）；句意为即便在考试周，他的书桌也保持整洁。图中可辨识物件：书桌、书本、笔。

pos.zh: 整洁的；简洁巧妙的；纯的；小巧匀称的

derivatives.zh: 由 neat 加 -ly 构成，义为「整齐地；干净利落地」
由 neat 加 -ness 构成，义为「整洁；工整」
由 neat 加 -en 构成，义为「把……收拾整齐」

senses.title: Tidy and in good order
senses.definition: arranged carefully, with everything in its place and no clutter
senses.definitionCN: 摆放得仔细，各在其位，没有杂乱
senses.example: His desk stayed neat even during the exam week.
senses.exampleCN: 即便在考试周，他的书桌也保持整洁。
senses.why: The word came into English from French net, clean and bright, and its first job was to describe a surface with nothing spoiling it; order was the visible proof of that cleanliness.
senses.whyCN: 这个词从法语 net 进入英语，本义是「干净、明亮」，最初形容没有污损的表面；整齐有序就是这种干净看得见的证据。

senses.title: Simple and skilfully done
senses.titleCN: 简洁巧妙的；干净利落的
senses.definition: done with care and skill so that the result is simple, exact and easy to follow
senses.definitionCN: 做得细致而有技巧，结果简单、准确、容易把握
senses.example: She found a neat solution that saved everyone an hour.
senses.exampleCN: 她想出一个简洁的办法，给每个人省下一小时。
senses.why: A surface is neat when nothing extra is on it, and a plan is neat when nothing extra is in it; the same dislike of clutter moves from tables to arguments.
senses.whyCN: 表面整洁是因为上面没有多余的东西，方案简洁是因为里面没有多余的步骤；同一种对杂乱的排斥，从桌面移到了论证里。

senses.title: Drunk plain, without ice or water
senses.definition: used of strong drink served on its own, with nothing added
senses.definitionCN: 用于烈酒，指单喝、不兑任何东西
senses.example: He asked for a neat whisky and sat by the window.
senses.exampleCN: 他要了一杯不加冰的威士忌，坐在窗边。
senses.why: A glass with nothing added is clean in the same literal way, so the old adjective for an unspoiled surface was applied to a drink that has not been diluted.
senses.whyCN: 什么都没加的杯子，字面上同样「干净」，于是那个形容未受污损表面的旧形容词，被用到了没有兑水的酒上。

senses.title: Small, trim and well shaped
senses.definition: used of a person's body or build, meaning small, compact and pleasing in shape
senses.definitionCN: 用于人的身材，意为小巧、紧凑、比例好看
senses.example: The dancer had a neat figure and very straight posture.
senses.exampleCN: 那位舞者身材小巧匀称，姿态非常挺拔。
senses.why: A small object with clean lines looks finished rather than cramped, so neat came to praise a body built on a small scale but without awkwardness.
senses.whyCN: 线条干净的小物件看起来是完成品，而不是被挤小的；于是 neat 也用来称赞小巧却不显笨拙的身材。

intro.en: Neat came through French from a Latin adjective for something shining and polished, and English widened it from a clean surface to a clear plan and an undiluted drink.
intro.cn: neat 经法语来自一个表示「光亮、打磨过」的拉丁形容词，英语把它的词义从干净表面扩展到清晰方案与不兑水的酒。

items.en: Nitidus meant shining, bright and polished, and by extension elegant and refined in appearance.
items.cn: nitidus 意为光亮的、鲜明的、打磨过的，引申指外表雅致、精致。

items.en: The verb nitere meant to shine or to look bright, and it is the source of the adjective and of the whole family.
items.cn: 动词 nitere 意为发光、显得明亮，是这个形容词以及整族词的来源。

items.en: Old French net kept the sense of clean, clear and unspoiled, and dropped the Latin brightness into a plainer cleanliness.
items.cn: 古法语 net 保留「干净、清澈、未受污损」的意思，把拉丁语的「光亮」落成了更朴素的「干净」。

items.en: Middle English nete or neat described clean clothes, clear writing and a person who kept things in order.
items.cn: 中古英语 nete 或 neat 形容干净的衣服、清楚的字迹，以及把东西收拾得井井有条的人。

items.en: Modern English adds the praise of a simple plan, the serving of undiluted spirits and the description of a compact figure.
items.cn: 现代英语添上对简洁方案的称赞、对不兑水烈酒的用法，以及对小巧身材的描述。

note.en: The look-alike group holds the adverb, the noun and the verb built on neat; the near-meaning group holds adjectives for order and for a well-kept appearance.
note.cn: 形近组收由 neat 构成的副词、名词与动词；近义组收表示「有序」与「外表收拾得好」的形容词。

entries.definition: In a tidy or skilful way, made with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 以整齐或利落的方式；由 neat 加 -ly 构成。

entries.definition: The quality of being tidy or skilfully simple.
entries.definitionCN: 整洁或简洁巧妙的性质。

entries.definition: To make something tidy, formed with -en.
entries.definitionCN: 把某物收拾整齐；由 neat 加 -en 构成。

entries.definition: A mesh for catching things; only the spelling is close to neat.
entries.definitionCN: 用来捕捉东西的网；只是拼写与 neat 相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: Arranged with everything in place, often said of rooms and habits.
entries.definitionCN: 各物归位、摆放有序，常用于房间与习惯。

entries.definition: Following a clear arrangement or method, often of groups and procedures.
entries.definitionCN: 遵循清楚的安排或方法，多用于群体与程序。

entries.definition: Neat and well shaped, especially of a person or a garden.
entries.definitionCN: 整齐而外形好看，尤指人或花园。

entries.definition: Smart and clean in appearance, usually of a person dressed well.
entries.definitionCN: 外表利落干净，通常指穿着得体的人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a French cleaning word with a Latin shine behind it, and its senses all keep some idea of nothing extra.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是法语中表示「干净」的词，背后有拉丁语的「光亮」，各个义项都带着「没有多余之物」的意思。

normal.en: French net meant clean and bright, and English kept the meaning but changed the spelling to neat.
normal.cn: 法语 net 意为干净、明亮，英语保留了意思，只把拼写改成 neat。

normal.en: Latin nitidus, shining, stands behind the French word, so neat and nitid share one old picture of a polished surface.
normal.cn: 拉丁语 nitidus（光亮的）站在法语词背后，所以 neat 与 nitid 共享一幅打磨过的表面画面。

normal.en: Neatly is the adverb, neatness the noun, neaten the verb; the family adds endings rather than new stems.
normal.cn: neatly 是副词，neatness 是名词，neaten 是动词；这一族只加词尾，不换词干。

normal.en: A neat solution is praised for having no extra steps, which is the same judgement as a neat desk with no extra papers.
normal.cn: a neat solution 被称赞是因为没有多余步骤，这与「没有多余纸张的整洁书桌」是同一种判断。

normal.en: Neat whisky has nothing added, so the clean-surface sense survives most literally in the glass.
normal.cn: neat whisky 什么都不加，所以「干净表面」这层意思在酒杯里保留得最字面。

abstract.en: Cleanliness, brightness and order turn out to be three views of one surface with nothing on it that should not be there.
abstract.cn: 干净、光亮与有序，其实只是同一个表面的三个视角：上面没有不该有的东西。

abstract.en: A word that began by praising a polished table ends up praising a proof with no wasted line.
abstract.cn: 一个从称赞打磨过的桌面开始的词，最后用来称赞没有一句废话的证明。

abstract.en: Serving a drink neat is the same compliment as keeping a desk neat: nothing has been added.
abstract.cn: 把酒纯着端上来，与把桌子收拾整齐是同一种称赞：什么都没有往里加。

examples.en: Her handwriting is small and very neat.
examples.cn: 她的字小而工整。

examples.en: He keeps his tools in a neat row on the shelf.
examples.cn: 他把工具在架子上排成整齐的一列。

examples.en: The team needed a neat way to explain the result.
examples.cn: 团队需要一个简洁的方式来解释这个结果。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「尼特」——东西摆得利落，一眼看过去清清爽爽；neat 就是整洁的。

root: 古法语 net（干净、明亮）来自拉丁语 nitidus（光亮的），一般认为与动词 nitere（发光）同源；本义「干净明亮」，后引申出整洁、简洁、纯饮与小巧诸义。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a surface with nothing extra on it; order, simplicity, an undiluted drink and a compact figure are four ways that emptiness of extras shows itself.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「没有多余之物的表面」；有序、简洁、不兑水的酒与小巧的身材，是这种「无多余」显现出来的四种方式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: books standing in one straight line on a desk, pens all pointing the same way.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上的书排成一条直线，笔尖全都朝着同一个方向。

branches.en: a shelf where every tool has its place
branches.cn: 每件工具都有位置的架子

branches.en: a page of writing without a smudge
branches.cn: 没有一处污痕的字页

branches.en: a proof that fits on one blackboard
branches.cn: 一块黑板就写得下的证明

branches.en: a glass filled and left alone
branches.cn: 斟满之后不再动的一只杯子

branches.en: a dancer standing very straight
branches.cn: 站得笔直的舞者

intro.en: The word is a French adjective of cleanliness, a Latin adjective of shine, and the English endings that turn it into adverb, noun and verb.
intro.cn: 这个词由法语表示「干净」的形容词、拉丁语表示「光亮」的形容词，以及把它变成副词、名词与动词的英语词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplied the adjective of shine and the verb behind it, and French passed the cleaned-up sense to English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了表示「光亮」的形容词及其动词，法语把「干净」这层意思传给了英语。

items.meaningCN: 光亮的；打磨过的；雅致的

items.meaning: in a tidy or skilful way

latinEntries.meaningCN: 光亮的；打磨过的；整洁的

definition_zh: 必然地；必定；不可避免地；不一定（用于 not necessarily）
definition_en: in a way that cannot be avoided or that follows with logical certainty; also used in the phrase not necessarily to deny that something is always true
core_image: 一条被两端拉紧的锁链，中间没有可以退让的余地
scene: 山道上的碎石还湿着，跑得太急的人收不住脚，一定会摔下去。If you run down a wet slope, you will necessarily fall.
sceneCN: 这里「necessarily」是「必然地、必定」（第 1 个义项：由逻辑或事实逼出来的结果）；句意是跑下湿滑斜坡的人必然会摔倒。图中可辨识物件：湿漉漉的碎石、斜坡、收不住的脚步。

pos.zh: 必然地；必定；不可避免地

derivatives.zh: 与 necessarily 同出于拉丁 necessarius，义为「必要的；必然的」
由拉丁 necessitas 进入英语，义为「必要性；必然性」
由 necessity 加动词后缀 -ate 构成，义为「使成为必要」

senses.title: As a logical certainty
senses.definition: in a way that follows by logic, so that no other result is possible
senses.definitionCN: 按逻辑推演下来必然如此，不可能有别的结果
senses.example: A triangle necessarily has three sides.
senses.exampleCN: 三角形必然有三条边。
senses.why: Latin necesse joined ne, not, with cedere, to give way: what cannot give way cannot be escaped, so the adverb states a result that logic or fact forces.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 necesse 把「不」与「退让」拼在一起：不肯退让的东西就躲不开，所以这个副词说的是逻辑或事实逼出来的结果。

senses.title: In every case, without exception
senses.titleCN: 不可避免地；每次都如此
senses.definition: in a way that happens in all cases, because the circumstances leave no room for an alternative
senses.definitionCN: 在所有情形下都会发生，因为客观条件没有留下别的可能
senses.example: When demand outruns supply, prices necessarily rise.
senses.exampleCN: 当需求超过供给，价格必然上涨。
senses.why: The same picture of a chain with no slack moves from one deduction to a general rule: once the conditions hold, the outcome cannot be held back.
senses.whyCN: 同一幅「锁链没有余量」的画面，从单次推论扩展到普遍规律：条件一旦成立，结果就压不住。

senses.title: Not in every case, in the phrase not necessarily
senses.definition: used after not to say that something is possible but not always or not certainly true
senses.definitionCN: 用在 not 之后，表示某事有可能，但并非总是或并非一定成立
senses.example: A quiet student is not necessarily a bored one.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的学生不一定就是觉得无聊。
senses.why: Negating a word of absolute certainty leaves a deliberate gap: the link may hold sometimes, but it is not forced, so the phrase warns against a hasty conclusion.
senses.whyCN: 把表示绝对必然的词一否定，就留下一个刻意的空隙：这种联系有时成立，却不是被逼出来的，所以这个说法是在提醒人别急着下结论。

intro.en: Necessarily is the adverb built on necessary, and the two words share one Latin idea: a necessity that cannot be pushed aside.
intro.cn: necessarily 是由 necessary 加 -ly 构成的副词，两词共享同一个拉丁观念：一种推不开的必然。

items.en: A negative particle and a root for yielding are generally reconstructed behind the Latin family, though the exact earlier shape is debated.
items.cn: 一般认为拉丁语这一族词的背后有一个否定小词和一个表示「退让」的词根，但更早的具体形式仍有争议。

items.en: Latin necesse meant unavoidable or inevitable; a common account reads it as ne, not, plus cedere, to give way.
items.cn: 拉丁语 necesse 意为不可避免、必然；一种常见解释是 ne（不）加 cedere（退让）。

items.en: The adjective necessarius described what one cannot do without, carrying the idea of an unyielding necessity into everyday need.
items.cn: 形容词 necessarius 描述离不开的东西，把「不肯退让的必然」带进了日常的「需要」。

items.en: Middle English used necessarie for what must be, and the adverb grew beside it with the ending -ly.
items.cn: 中古英语用 necessarie 表示「必须如此的」，副词形式随后加 -ly 长出来。

items.en: Modern English keeps necessarily for logical and practical certainty, and the negative phrase not necessarily for the deliberate exception.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 necessarily 表示逻辑与事实上的确定，并用否定短语 not necessarily 表示刻意留下的例外。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin family and its English endings; the near-meaning group gathers adverbs of certainty and of unavoidable occurrence.
note.cn: 形近组沿着拉丁词族与英语词尾展开；近义组收表示确定与不可避免发生的副词。

entries.definition: The adjective behind the adverb, meaning needed or certain.
entries.definitionCN: 副词背后的形容词，义为「必要的；必然的」。

entries.definition: The state or quality of being necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 必要性；必然性。

entries.definition: To make something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要。

entries.definition: In a way that is not needed.
entries.definitionCN: 以不必要的方式。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be prevented.
entries.definitionCN: 不可避免地；终究会。

entries.definition: In a way that cannot be escaped.
entries.definitionCN: 无法避免地。

entries.definition: Without doubt; for sure.
entries.definitionCN: 无疑地；肯定地。

normalIntro.en: The word carries a Latin refusal to budge, and its family keeps turning that refusal into logical certainty and practical necessity.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「不肯让步」的劲头，同族词不断把这种不肯让步变成逻辑上的确定与现实中的必需。

normal.en: Necesse is read as ne plus cedere, so the core picture is something that will not give way.
normal.cn: necesse 可拆成 ne 加 cedere，核心画面就是一件不肯退让的东西。

normal.en: The suffix -ly turns the adjective necessary into the adverb necessarily, just as it turns quick into quickly.
normal.cn: -ly 把形容词 necessary 变成副词 necessarily，就像把 quick 变成 quickly。

normal.en: Not necessarily does not cancel the word; it denies that the link holds in every case.
normal.cn: not necessarily 并没有取消这个词，它否认的是这种联系在每种情况下都成立。

normal.en: Necessity and necessitate are relatives: one names the state, the other the act of making something necessary.
normal.cn: necessity 与 necessitate 是同族词：一个指状态，一个指使某事成为必要的动作。

normal.en: In a proof, necessarily marks the step that no counterexample can overturn.
normal.cn: 在证明里，necessarily 标出的是任何反例都推不翻的那一步。

abstract.en: A chain tightened at both ends is a good picture of a conclusion that cannot be loosened by argument.
abstract.cn: 两端拉紧的锁链，很适合形容一个怎么争辩都松不开的结论。

abstract.en: The negative phrase works like a small door left open in an otherwise closed wall.
abstract.cn: 那个否定短语就像一堵封闭的墙上故意留下的一扇小门。

abstract.en: Every time the word appears, someone is claiming that the room for choice has shrunk to nothing.
abstract.cn: 这个词每次出现，都有人在声称可供选择的空间已经缩到没有。

examples.en: A triangle necessarily has three sides.
examples.cn: 三角形必然有三条边。

examples.en: When demand outruns supply, prices necessarily rise.
examples.cn: 当需求超过供给，价格必然上涨。

examples.en: A quiet student is not necessarily a bored one.
examples.cn: 安静的学生不一定就是觉得无聊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢色塞热利」——听着像一串含糊的尾音，意思却是躲不开的必然；记住 necessarily 是必然地。

root: 拉丁语 necesse（不可避免）一般认为由否定成分 ne- 与 cedere（退让）构成；加 -arius 得 necessarius，再加 -ly 成为 necessarily。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a necessity that will not yield; the senses divide into logical certainty, universal occurrence, and the negated phrase that keeps one exception alive.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一种不肯退让的必然；义项分出逻辑上的确定、普遍发生的情形，以及保留一个例外的否定说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a chain pulled tight at both ends, with no slack left in the middle.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条两端拉紧的锁链，中间不留一点余量。

branches.en: a proof that closes every other door one by one
branches.cn: 证明把其他可能的门一扇扇关掉

branches.en: three sides that cannot be counted otherwise
branches.cn: 三条边怎么数都改不了

branches.en: a price climbing because supply has run short
branches.cn: 供给短缺，价格随之上抬

branches.en: a calm face read as boredom without proof
branches.cn: 凭一张平静的脸就断定人家无聊

branches.en: a question answered with a careful maybe
branches.cn: 一个问题只得到谨慎的「也许」

intro.en: One Latin adjective of necessity, its negative and verbal parts, and two English endings hold this entry together.
intro.cn: 一个表示必然的拉丁形容词、它的否定与动词成分，以及两个英语词尾共同撑起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: Latin supplies the whole family: necesse, its adjective necessarius and the verb cedere behind the negative element.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语提供了整族词：necesse、它的形容词 necessarius，以及藏在否定成分背后的动词 cedere。

definition_zh: 必要的；必需的；必然的；必需品（常用复数 necessaries）
definition_en: needed so that something can be done or achieved; certain to happen as a result; and, as a plural noun, the things a person needs
core_image: 一把钥匙插进锁孔，门后是缺了它就办不成的那件事
scene: 出发前一晚，队长把清单摊在木桌上逐项核对，缺了任何一样队伍都走不成。A map and a compass are necessary for the route they have chosen.
sceneCN: 这里「necessary」是「必要的、必需的」（第 1 个义项：缺了就无法完成某事）；句意是地图和指南针是他们所选路线必需的装备。图中可辨识物件：木桌上的清单、地图、指南针。

derivatives.zh: 由拉丁 necessitas 进入英语，义为「必要性；必然性；必需品」
由 necessary 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「必然地」
由 necessary 加否定前缀 un- 构成，义为「不必要的」

senses.title: Needed for a purpose
senses.definition: required so that something can happen or be achieved
senses.definitionCN: 为了做成某事而不可缺少的
senses.example: Water is necessary for every living cell.
senses.exampleCN: 水对每个活细胞来说都是必需的。
senses.why: Latin necessarius first meant what cannot be avoided; English moved that force into the practical sphere, where it marks what cannot be left out.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 necessarius 最初指躲不开的东西；英语把这份强制感移进日常事务，用来标出不能漏掉的那一项。

senses.title: Certain to follow as a result
senses.definition: certain to happen as a result of something else, with no real alternative
senses.definitionCN: 作为另一件事的结果必定发生，没有别的可能
senses.example: A rise in temperature is a necessary result of the reaction.
senses.exampleCN: 温度上升是这场反应的必然结果。
senses.why: If a thing cannot be avoided, it can also be called necessary as a consequence: the cause leaves the effect no room to differ.
senses.whyCN: 一件事既躲不开，也就可以作为结果被称为必然：原因没给结果留下任何差异的余地。

senses.title: Things a person cannot do without
senses.definition: the items a person needs for daily life, usually used in the plural form
senses.definitionCN: 日常生活离不开的物品，通常用复数形式
senses.example: The family packed only the necessaries for the winter.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人只收拾了过冬最基本的必需品。
senses.why: An adjective turns into a noun when English wants to name the objects that carry the quality; the plural marks a set of such objects rather than one.
senses.whyCN: 当英语想直接称呼带有这种性质的物件时，形容词就变成名词；复数标记的是一整套这样的东西，而不是单件。

intro.en: Necessary reached English through French from Latin, and its root idea is not simply wanted but impossible to avoid.
intro.cn: necessary 经法语从拉丁语进入英语，它的根义不是「想要」，而是「避不开」。

items.en: Behind the Latin word lie a negative particle and a root for yielding, though the exact prehistoric form is not settled.
items.cn: 这个拉丁词的背后有一个否定小词和一个表示退让的词根，但更早的确切形式尚无定论。

items.en: Latin necesse meant unavoidable; one widely repeated account divides it into ne, not, and cedere, to give way.
items.cn: 拉丁语 necesse 意为不可避免；一种流传很广的解释把它分成 ne（不）与 cedere（退让）。

items.en: The adjective necessarius described what one cannot do without and passed both necessity and practical need to later languages.
items.cn: 形容词 necessarius 指离不开的东西，把「必然」与「实际需要」一起传给了后世语言。

items.en: Old French necessaire carried the word to England after the Norman conquest, where it was spelled in several ways.
items.cn: 古法语 necessaire 在诺曼征服后把这个词带到英格兰，当时拼写有好几种。

items.en: Modern English uses necessary for what is required and for what must follow, and the plural noun for the bare items of daily life.
items.cn: 现代英语用 necessary 既指「必需」也指「必然」，复数名词则指日常生活里最基本的那些东西。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the same Latin stem and its endings; the near-meaning group gathers adjectives for what cannot be done without.
note.cn: 形近组沿同一拉丁词干及其词尾展开；近义组收表示「缺了就不行」的形容词。

entries.definition: The adverb formed from necessary with -ly.
entries.definitionCN: 由 necessary 加 -ly 构成的副词。

entries.definition: The state of being necessary, or a thing that is needed.
entries.definitionCN: 必要性；必需品。

entries.definition: To make something necessary.
entries.definitionCN: 使某事成为必要。

entries.definition: Not needed; more than is required.
entries.definitionCN: 不必要的；多余的。

entries.definition: Absolutely needed for something to exist or work.
entries.definitionCN: 某物存在或运作绝对需要的。

entries.definition: Needed for life or for success.
entries.definitionCN: 生命或成功所必需的。

entries.definition: Demanded by a rule or by the situation.
entries.definitionCN: 规则或情形所要求的。

entries.definition: Too important to be done without.
entries.definitionCN: 重要到不可缺少的。

normalIntro.en: The word is a Latin refusal to yield, put to work in shopping lists, rules and consequences; the family keeps that double life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词本是拉丁语里「不肯退让」的劲头，后来被用在清单、规则和结果上，同族词一直保留这双重身份。

normal.en: Necesse carries the sense of what will not give way, which is why necessary can mean both required and certain.
normal.cn: necesse 带着「不肯让步」的意味，所以 necessary 既能指「必需」，也能指「必然」。

normal.en: The plural noun necessaries is old-fashioned but correct for a set of daily needs.
normal.cn: 复数名词 necessaries 虽显旧，但指一整套日常所需时是正确的。

normal.en: Unnecessary adds un-, and the word simply reverses: not needed rather than needed.
normal.cn: unnecessary 加了 un-，词义直接反转：不是必需，而是不必要。

normal.en: Necessity names the state, necessitate the act, and necessary the quality, all from one Latin base.
normal.cn: necessity 指状态，necessitate 指动作，necessary 指性质，三者同出一个拉丁词干。

normal.en: If necessary is a fixed phrase that shortens a whole conditional clause into two words.
normal.cn: if necessary 是固定说法，把一个完整条件句压缩成两个词。

abstract.en: A key that opens one door is necessary only because of that door; the word always implies a purpose behind the need.
abstract.cn: 一把钥匙之所以必需，是因为有那扇门；这个词背后总藏着一个目的。

abstract.en: A necessary result is a consequence with no side road, which is why the same adjective can sound like fate.
abstract.cn: 必然结果是一条没有岔路的结果，所以同一个形容词有时听起来像命运。

abstract.en: Calling things necessaries reduces a whole life to a short list of objects that must be carried.
abstract.cn: 把东西叫作 necessaries，等于把一整段生活压缩成一张必须携带的短清单。

examples.en: The repair is necessary before the bridge can reopen.
examples.cn: 桥要重新开放，先得完成这项维修。

examples.en: Sleep is necessary for the body to recover.
examples.cn: 睡眠对身体恢复是必要的。

examples.en: The shelter kept only the bare necessaries for the night.
examples.cn: 收容所只留了过夜最基本的必需品。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「呢色塞瑞」——必需品总在「呢色」堆里被翻出来；记住 necessary 是必要的、必然的。

root: 拉丁语 necesse（不可避免）一般认为由 ne-（不）与 cedere（退让）构成，派生形容词 necessarius；经古法语 necessaire 进入英语。

sensesIntro.en: The core is what cannot be done without; the senses then split into practical need, forced consequence, and the plural noun for the objects themselves.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「缺了就不行」；义项分出实际需要、被迫产生的结果，以及直接指物件本身的复数名词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a key turning in a lock that will not open without it.
core.cn: 核心意象：一把钥匙插进锁孔，没有它就打不开那扇门。

branches.en: a checklist with one item circled twice
branches.cn: 清单上有一项被圈了两遍

branches.en: a thermometer rising because the reaction has started
branches.cn: 反应开始后温度计一路上升

branches.en: a suitcase holding only soap, thread and a candle
branches.cn: 行李箱里只有肥皂、线团和一支蜡烛

branches.en: a bridge waiting for one last repair before traffic
branches.cn: 桥等着最后一项维修才放行

branches.en: a shop shelf marked for daily needs
branches.cn: 货架上标着日常所需的那一排

intro.en: A Latin negative, a verb of yielding, an adjective and two English endings build this entry from the inside out.
intro.cn: 一个拉丁否定成分、一个表示退让的动词、一个形容词和两个英语词尾，从内到外搭起这个词条。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is well recorded: necesse, its derived adjective necessarius, and the verb cedere that the negative element is thought to contain.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基有明确记载：necesse、由它派生的形容词 necessarius，以及一般认为藏在否定成分里的动词 cedere。

definition_zh: 颈；脖子；领口；（瓶、琴等的）细长颈部；地峡；拥吻
definition_en: the part of the body joining the head to the shoulders; a narrow joining part of an object; the opening of a garment; a narrow strip of land; and, informally, to kiss and hold someone closely
core_image: 一双手环绕在头与肩之间，把两端连成一条柔软的通道
scene: 入冬后风从领口灌进来，母亲把围巾绕过孩子颈后，又把垂下来的一端塞进外套。She wrapped the scarf around the child's neck and tucked the loose end into his coat.
sceneCN: 这里「neck」是「脖子、颈部」（第 1 个义项：连接头与肩的身体部位）；句意是母亲把围巾绕在孩子脖子上，把垂下的一端塞进外套。图中可辨识物件：围巾、外套、被风掀起的领口。

pos.zh: 颈；脖子；领口；细长颈部；地峡

derivatives.zh: 由 neck 与 line 复合而成，义为「领口线；领口」
由 neck 与 lace 复合而成，义为「项链」
由 turtle 与 neck 复合而成，义为「高领；高领毛衣」

senses.title: The part joining the head to the body
senses.definition: the narrow part of the body that connects the head to the shoulders and chest
senses.definitionCN: 连接头部与肩胸之间那段较窄的身体部位
senses.example: The cat rubbed its neck against the door frame.
senses.exampleCN: 猫把脖子蹭在门框上。
senses.why: Old English hnecca named the narrow bridge between head and trunk; the shape of a constriction between two wider ends is what the word first points at.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 hnecca 指的就是头与躯干之间那条窄窄的桥；这个词最早指向的是「两端宽、中间收窄」的形状。

senses.title: A narrow joining part of an object
senses.definition: the long narrow part of an object, such as a bottle or a stringed instrument, that joins it to the rest
senses.definitionCN: 瓶子、弦乐器等物件上细长的连接部分
senses.example: The label was glued around the neck of the bottle.
senses.exampleCN: 标签被粘在瓶颈上。
senses.why: Any object shaped like that bridge lends its narrow joining part the same name, because the picture is a constriction between two wider ends.
senses.whyCN: 任何物件只要长得像那条桥，它的细长连接处就借用了同一个名字，因为画面仍是「两端宽、中间收」。

senses.title: The opening of a garment
senses.definition: the part of a shirt, dress or sweater that surrounds the neck and is shaped to fit it
senses.definitionCN: 衬衫、连衣裙或毛衣上围着脖子、按颈部形状裁出的开口
senses.example: She pulled the sweater down over a wide neck.
senses.exampleCN: 她把毛衣往下拉，盖住宽大的领口。
senses.why: The garment opening sits exactly where the body's neck passes through, so the word transfers from the body to the cloth that surrounds it.
senses.whyCN: 衣服的开口正好位于脖子穿过的地方，于是这个词从身体转到了包住身体的那层布上。

senses.title: A narrow strip of land between waters
senses.definition: a narrow piece of land that joins two larger areas of land and has water on either side
senses.definitionCN: 连接两片较大陆地、两侧临水的狭长地带
senses.example: The village stood on a low neck of land between two bays.
senses.exampleCN: 村子坐落在两个海湾之间一块低矮的地峡上。
senses.why: A strip of land with water on both sides looks like a narrow joining piece, so the same word is used for an isthmus.
senses.whyCN: 两侧临水的一条陆地，看起来就像一块窄窄的连接件，所以同一个词也被用来指地峡。

senses.title: To kiss and hold someone closely, in informal use
senses.definition: in informal speech, to kiss and caress someone while holding them close
senses.definitionCN: 口语中表示搂着某人亲吻、抚摸
senses.example: Two teenagers were necking on a bench by the lake.
senses.exampleCN: 两个少年在湖边的长椅上拥吻。
senses.why: Two people holding each other head to head put their necks close together, and English took the body part as a verb for that embrace.
senses.whyCN: 两个人耳鬓相贴地抱在一起时，脖子挨得最近；英语便拿这个身体部位作动词，指这种拥抱。

intro.en: Neck is a Germanic body word whose deeper origin is uncertain, and it has spread from the body to bottles, clothes and land.
intro.cn: neck 是日耳曼语的身体词，更早的来源不确定；它从身体扩展到瓶子、衣服和土地。

items.en: The deeper origin is uncertain; some accounts link the Germanic word to a root for bending or pressing together, but this is not settled.
items.cn: 更早的来源不确定；有说法把它与表示「弯曲、压紧」的词根联系起来，但并未定论。

items.en: A reconstructed form such as hnakkaz is generally given for the Germanic word for the back of the neck.
items.cn: 一般认为日耳曼语中表示颈背的词有一个类似 hnakkaz 的重构形式。

items.en: Old English hnecca named the neck or nape, and the initial hn- was still pronounced at that stage.
items.cn: 古英语 hnecca 指颈或颈背，当时词首的 hn- 还要发音。

items.en: Middle English dropped the initial h and wrote nekke, the shape that leads towards the modern spelling.
items.cn: 中古英语去掉了词首的 h，写作 nekke，这个形状一路通向现代拼写。

items.en: Modern English keeps neck for the body part and extends it to narrow parts of objects, the opening of clothes, a strip of land and an informal verb.
items.cn: 现代英语保留 neck 指身体部位，并扩展到物件细长处、衣服开口、狭长陆地，还多了一个口语动词。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds in which the word survives; the near-meaning group collects neighbouring body and clothing terms.
note.cn: 形近组收仍保留这个词的复合词；近义组收相邻的身体部位与衣着用语。

entries.definition: The line or shape of a garment's opening at the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 衣服领口的线条或形状。

entries.definition: A string of beads or metal worn around the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 戴在脖子上的珠串或金属饰物。

entries.definition: A high collar that covers the neck, or a sweater with one.
entries.definitionCN: 遮住脖子的高领，或带高领的毛衣。

entries.definition: The narrow neck of a bottle, or a point where traffic or work slows down.
entries.definitionCN: 瓶颈；交通或工作中的阻塞点。

entries.definition: The passage inside the neck, used for breathing and swallowing.
entries.definitionCN: 颈部内部用于呼吸和吞咽的通道。

entries.definition: The part of a shirt that stands up around the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 衬衫上围着脖子的那一圈。

entries.definition: The back of the neck.
entries.definitionCN: 颈背；后颈。

normalIntro.en: One Old English body word, a lost h, and a habit of naming any narrow join after it: that is the whole history in brief.
normalIntro.cn: 一个古英语身体词、一个消失的 h，以及见到窄连接处就借用的习惯，就是这段历史的大概。

normal.en: Old English hnecca began with hn-, and Middle English simply dropped the h to give nekke.
normal.cn: 古英语 hnecca 以 hn- 开头，中古英语直接把 h 去掉，成了 nekke。

normal.en: Neckline and necklace are compounds that keep the body sense: the line and the jewellery both sit at the neck.
normal.cn: neckline 与 necklace 都是保留身体义的复合词：领口线和首饰都落在脖子处。

normal.en: A bottleneck borrows the shape, not the body: a bottle's narrow part holds traffic or work back.
normal.cn: bottleneck 借的是形状而不是身体：瓶子的细处把交通或工作卡住。

normal.en: Neck and neck pictures two horses whose heads are level, hence the meaning 'exactly equal'.
normal.cn: neck and neck 想像两匹马齐头并进，于是有了「不相上下」的意思。

normal.en: Break one's neck is violent in form but often means rushing dangerously fast.
normal.cn: break one's neck 字面很凶，实际常指拼命赶路、快得危险。

abstract.en: The neck is where a large head is balanced on a narrow support, which is why the word suits any risky narrow join.
abstract.cn: 脖子是让大脑袋架在窄支柱上的地方，所以这个词也适合任何危险的窄连接处。

abstract.en: A garment opening and a body part share one name because cloth is cut to follow the body it covers.
abstract.cn: 衣服开口与身体部位共用一个名字，因为布料是照着它所覆盖的身体裁出来的。

abstract.en: A neck of land is a place where two large worlds touch through a thin corridor.
abstract.cn: 地峡是两片大世界通过一条细走廊相接的地方。

examples.en: The cat rubbed its neck against the door frame.
examples.cn: 猫把脖子蹭在门框上。

examples.en: The label was glued around the neck of the bottle.
examples.cn: 标签被粘在瓶颈上。

examples.en: Two teenagers were necking on a bench by the lake.
examples.cn: 两个少年在湖边的长椅上拥吻。

root: 古英语 hnecca（颈；颈背），一般认为源自原始日耳曼语重构形式 hnakkaz，更早的印欧语来源不确定；同族词有 neckline、necklace、turtleneck 等。

sensesIntro.en: The core is a narrow bridge between two wider parts; the senses divide into the body part, narrow parts of objects, a garment opening, a strip of land, and the informal embrace.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是两块宽处之间的窄桥；义项分出身体部位、物件细长处、衣服开口、狭长陆地，以及口语里的拥抱亲吻。

core.cn: 核心意象：一双手环住头部与两肩之间那段窄窄的空间。

intro.en: The entry is built from one Old English noun, an English verb, its endings, and compounds that keep the body sense alive.
intro.cn: 这个词条由一个古英语名词、一个英语动词、它的词尾，以及让身体义延续的复合词搭成。

latinIntro.en: The word is Germanic; Latin cervix, the word for neck, belongs to a different root, so no reliable Latin cognate is listed here.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词属日耳曼语族；拉丁语里表示颈的 cervix 属于另一个词根，所以这里不列可靠的拉丁同族词。

definition_zh: 需要；需求；贫困
definition_en: to require something, or a thing that is required, or a state of great poverty
core_image: 雨天里孩子发现忘带伞，站在校门口望着雨帘
scene: 雨天里孩子发现忘带伞，站在校门口望着雨帘。I need a pen for the test.

senses.title: To require something
senses.definition: To require something
senses.definitionCN: 必须有某物
senses.example: I need a pen for the test.
senses.exampleCN: 考试我需要一支笔。
senses.why: Old English neodian meant to have to have something; the verb keeps that plain sense of lack and requirement.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 neodian 意为必须有某物，动词保留了欠缺与必需的本义。

senses.title: A thing that is required
senses.definition: A thing that is required
senses.definitionCN: 必需之物
senses.example: The town has a need for more doctors.
senses.exampleCN: 这个镇需要更多医生。
senses.why: The verb became a noun naming the lack itself and what would fill it.
senses.whyCN: 动词转为名词，指欠缺本身以及能填补它的东西。

senses.title: A state of great poverty
senses.definition: A state of great poverty
senses.definitionCN: 极度缺乏的状态
senses.example: The family is in great need.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人非常贫困。
senses.why: When the lack covers food and shelter, need names hardship, not just a missing object.
senses.whyCN: 当欠缺涉及食物与住所，need 就指困苦，而不只是少了一件东西。

intro.en: The history of need is traced through the stages below; thin evidence is marked as such.
intro.cn: need 的历史按下面几个阶段追溯；证据不足处如实标注。

items.cn: 名词指需求本身。

items.en: Need covers verb, noun and hardship.
items.cn: 现代英语中它涵盖动词、名词与困苦。

definition_zh: 否定的；负面的；消极的；负的；负数；底片
definition_en: saying no or refusing; harmful or unwelcome; less than zero; and, as a noun, a number below zero, a film image with light and dark reversed, or a denying word
core_image: 一个减号落在数字前面，把整条刻度推向另一边
scene: 实验记录摊在桌上，最后一列数字前面都带着减号，组长让大家重新核对每一根接线。The meter gave a negative reading, so the team checked every connection again.
sceneCN: 这里「negative」是「负的、负数的」（第 3 个义项：小于零的数值）；句意是仪表给出负值，于是全组把每处接线重新查了一遍。图中可辨识物件：实验记录、减号、仪表、接线。

derivatives.zh: 由 negative 加副词后缀 -ly 构成，义为「否定地；负面地」
由 negative 加名词后缀 -ity 构成，义为「消极性；负面情绪」

senses.title: Saying no or refusing
senses.definition: expressing refusal or denial, rather than agreement
senses.definitionCN: 表示拒绝或否认，而不是同意
senses.example: She gave a negative answer without looking up.
senses.exampleCN: 她头也没抬，给了一个否定的回答。
senses.why: Latin negare meant to say no, and the adjective negativus simply carried that refusal into a describing word.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 negare 意为说「不」，形容词 negativus 只是把这份拒绝带进描述性的词里。

senses.title: Harmful, unwelcome or pessimistic
senses.definition: having a bad or harmful effect, or showing a lack of hope and confidence
senses.definitionCN: 带来不良或有害影响，或表现出缺少希望与信心
senses.example: The new rules had a negative effect on small shops.
senses.exampleCN: 新规定对小店铺产生了负面影响。
senses.why: A refusal pushes something away, and what is pushed away is often felt as harm; from 'saying no' the word slides to 'working against you'.
senses.whyCN: 拒绝就是把某物推开，而被推开的东西往往让人觉得有害；于是词义从「说不」滑向「对你不利」。

senses.title: Less than zero
senses.definition: below zero on a scale, or represented with a minus sign
senses.definitionCN: 刻度上小于零，或用减号表示
senses.example: Minus five is a negative number.
senses.exampleCN: 负五是一个负数。
senses.why: A minus sign reverses direction on a number line, so the word for denial also marks values that fall on the other side of zero.
senses.whyCN: 减号在数轴上把方向反过来，所以表示否认的词也用来标记落在零另一边的数值。

senses.title: A film image with light and dark reversed
senses.definition: a piece of film or paper on which light and dark, and often colours, are reversed
senses.definitionCN: 明暗乃至颜色被反转的胶片或相纸
senses.example: He kept the old negatives in a paper envelope.
senses.exampleCN: 他把旧底片收在一个纸信封里。
senses.why: In a photographic negative the picture is turned inside out, bright sky becoming dark; the word names that reversal, which is its oldest visual sense.
senses.whyCN: 在照相底片上，画面是反过来的，明亮的天空变成暗色；这个词命名的正是这种反转，也是它最古老的视觉义。

intro.en: Negative comes from a Latin verb for saying no, and the idea of reversal runs through denial, harm, below-zero values and film.
intro.cn: negative 出自拉丁语中表示说「不」的动词，「反转」这个观念贯穿否认、损害、零下数值与胶片。

items.en: A reconstructed negative particle lies far behind the Latin family for denying, though its exact form is not certain.
items.cn: 拉丁语这一族表示否认的词，远处可追到一个重构的否定小词，但其确切形式并不确定。

items.en: negare meant to say no, to refuse or deny; how its internal parts were formed is still debated.
items.cn: negare 意为说「不」、拒绝或否认；它内部如何构成至今仍有争论。

items.en: negativus was the adjective for denying or refusing, built on the stem with the ending -ivus.
items.cn: negativus 是表示否认或拒绝的形容词，由词干加 -ivus 构成。

items.en: Middle English took negatif from French and used it first for a statement that denies something.
items.cn: 中古英语从法语借来 negatif，最早用来指否定某事的陈述。

items.en: Modern English widens negative to harmful effects, numbers below zero and the reversed image on film.
items.cn: 现代英语把 negative 扩展到有害影响、零以下数值，以及胶片上反转的画面。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the Latin verb of denial and its endings; the near-meaning group gathers words for harm, refusal and their opposites.
note.cn: 形近组沿拉丁语表示否认的动词及其词尾展开；近义组收表示损害、拒绝以及相反概念的词。

normalIntro.en: The word begins with a Latin no and ends by marking anything turned the other way: a reply, an effect, a number, a photograph.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词从拉丁语的「不」出发，最后用来标记一切被翻到另一面的东西：回答、影响、数字、照片。

normal.en: Negare is the Latin verb 'to deny', and negativus is its adjective, so the family is regular once the verb is known.
normal.cn: negare 是拉丁语「否认」动词，negativus 是它的形容词；记住动词，这一族词就顺了。

normal.en: The prefix neg- carries the sense of no, the same element heard in negate and negation.
normal.cn: neg- 这个成分带着「不」的意思，在 negate 与 negation 里也能听到。

normal.en: Negative feedback does not mean bad feedback; it means feedback that pushes back against the current state.
normal.cn: negative feedback 不是「坏反馈」，而是往回压、抵消当前状态的那种反馈。

normal.en: In the negative is a formal way of saying that the answer is no.
normal.cn: in the negative 是「回答是否定的」的正式说法。

normal.en: A photographic negative reverses light and dark, which makes the word's idea of reversal visible.
normal.cn: 照相底片把明暗反过来，让这个词的「反转」观念看得见。

abstract.en: A minus sign is a small mark that flips the whole direction of a number, much like a single no can flip a decision.
abstract.cn: 一个减号就能把数字的方向整个翻过来，很像一句「不」能翻掉一个决定。

abstract.en: Calling an effect negative is a way of saying it pushes against what we wanted.
abstract.cn: 把某种影响叫作负面，等于说它顶着我们想要的方向推。

abstract.en: The film negative stores a picture by keeping the opposite of every light and shadow.
abstract.cn: 底片靠保存每处明暗的相反值来存下一幅画面。

examples.en: The new rules had a negative effect on small shops.

examples.en: Minus five is a negative number.
examples.cn: 负五是一个负数。

sensesIntro.cn: 核心是一句把事物翻到另一面的「不」；义项分出拒绝、损害、零以下数值，以及反转的照相影像。

definition_en: to discuss something in order to reach an agreement, or to get past a difficulty, a stretch of ground or a financial instrument

senses.title: Discuss in order to agree
senses.titleCN: 为达成一致而反复商谈
senses.definition: to talk with another party, trading proposals, until a shared position is reached
senses.definitionCN: 与另一方来回提出方案，直到达成共同的立场
senses.example: Union and management negotiated for eleven hours.
senses.exampleCN: 工会与资方谈了十一个小时。
senses.why: the Latin source means carrying on business, and bargaining is business conducted in words.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词源意为「做买卖」，而讨价还价正是用言语做的买卖。

senses.title: Settle the terms of a deal
senses.definition: to settle a price, a contract or a release by bargaining
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨价还价把价格、合同或释放条件定下来
senses.example: The captain negotiated the release of the crew.
senses.exampleCN: 船长谈成了船员的释放。
senses.why: the verb shifts from the talking to its product: what has been agreed now exists as terms.
senses.whyCN: 这个动词从「谈」转向「谈出的结果」：已议定之事，如今作为条款存在。

senses.title: Get past a difficulty
senses.definition: to deal with an obstacle or a stage of a process successfully
senses.definitionCN: 成功地应付一处障碍或某个程序阶段
senses.example: The bill negotiated the committee stage intact.
senses.exampleCN: 这项法案完整地通过了委员会阶段。
senses.why: a difficulty is treated like a stretch of road: you do not remove it, you get through it.
senses.whyCN: 难题被当成一段路来看：你不拆掉它，而是穿过去。

senses.title: Cross rough ground
senses.definition: to travel over or through a difficult physical passage
senses.definitionCN: 从一段难走的实际通道上通过
senses.example: Mules negotiate the narrow ledge without hesitation.
senses.exampleCN: 骡子毫不犹豫地走过那道窄石檐。
senses.why: this is the most physical branch: the bargaining skill of finding a way through becomes walking through.
senses.whyCN: 这是最具体的一支：谈判中「找出一条路」的本事，变成了真的走过去。

senses.title: Transfer or cash a draft
senses.definition: of a cheque or bill, to pass it to another party for value
senses.definitionCN: 指支票或汇票被交给另一方以取得对价
senses.example: The bank refused to negotiate the draft.
senses.exampleCN: 银行拒绝兑付这张汇票。
senses.why: a bill of exchange is a promise passed from hand to hand, and the verb names that passing.
senses.whyCN: 汇票是一张在人与人之间传递的承诺，这个动词命名的正是这次传递。

senses.title: Carry on trade
senses.definition: to buy and sell, to conduct business, in the older commercial sense
senses.definitionCN: 买卖货物、经营生意，属较早的商业用法
senses.example: Merchants negotiated in spices and tin.
senses.exampleCN: 商人们在香料与锡之间做买卖。
senses.why: the original Latin verb meant exactly this; the diplomatic sense is the later narrowing.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁原动词正是这个意思；后来外交上的用法才是收窄出来的。

senses.title: Obtain by bargaining
senses.definition: to secure a benefit for oneself or others through bargaining
senses.definitionCN: 通过讨价还价为自己或他人争得某种好处
senses.example: She negotiated a shorter working week for the whole team.
senses.exampleCN: 她为整个团队争得了更短的工作周。
senses.why: negotiating is not only meeting the other side halfway; it is also extracting a concession from them.
senses.whyCN: 谈判不只是各让一步，也是从对方那里争得一项让步。

senses.title: Manage a passage successfully
senses.definition: to handle a vehicle or a situation through a hazardous passage
senses.definitionCN: 把车辆或局面稳稳地带过一段危险路程
senses.example: The pilot negotiated the storm with steady hands.
senses.exampleCN: 飞行员稳稳地把飞机带过了暴风雨。
senses.why: when the obstacle is weather or traffic, the word describes control rather than talking.
senses.whyCN: 当障碍是天气或车流时，这个词描述的是「掌控」，而不是「商谈」。

intro.en: Negotiate comes from Latin negotiari 'to carry on business', from negotium 'business', literally 'not-leisure'. The agreement sense is a later narrowing. Dates are approximate.
intro.cn: negotiate 来自拉丁 negotiari「做买卖」，其名词 negotium「事务、生意」字面是「不得闲」。表示「达成协议」的义项是后来收窄出来的。年代均为约数。

items.en: Negotium 'business, affair' was formed from neg- 'not' and otium 'leisure': business is the state in which one has no leisure.
items.cn: negotium「事务、生意」由 neg-「不」与 otium「闲暇」构成：生意就是「不得闲」的状态。

items.en: The deponent verb negotiari meant 'to carry on business, to trade', and negotiator named the merchant who did so.
items.cn: 异态动词 negotiari 意为「经营、买卖」，negotiatio 与 negotiator 分别指经商这件事与经商的商人。

items.en: English took the verb in the sixteenth century first in the commercial sense of trading and dealing.
items.cn: 英语在十六世纪借入这个动词，最初正是「做买卖、经营」的商业义。

items.en: The sense of conferring with someone, talking a matter over, appears next, still without any promise of agreement.
items.cn: 接着出现「与人商议、把事情谈一谈」的义项，当时仍不含达成协议的承诺。

items.en: Diplomacy fixed the modern sense: to confer with a view to reaching terms, and later to settle those terms.
items.cn: 外交用法固定了现代义：为议定条件而商谈，后来又指把这些条件谈成。

items.en: Source uncertain (first dates): the boundary between the conferring sense and the settling sense is dated differently in different dictionaries, and the earlier history of otium beyond Latin is a reconstruction.
items.cn: 来源不确定（首见年代）：各家词典对「商议」与「谈成」两义的分界年代说法不一；otium 在拉丁语之前的来历属重构形式。

note.en: Group one holds words that share the shape of the ending but come from unrelated Latin verbs; group two holds verbs that also settle matters between people.
note.cn: 第一组收词尾形状相同、却出自互不相干的拉丁动词的词；第二组收同样在人与人之间把事定下来的动词。

entries.definition: From Latin negare 'to deny', built on neg- 'not'; it means to deny or make ineffective, with no link to business.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 negare「否认」，由 neg-「不」构成；意为否定或使失效，与「生意」无关。

entries.definition: From Latin navigare, built on navis 'ship' plus agere 'drive'; it means to steer a course, not to bargain.
entries.definitionCN: 来自拉丁 navigare，由 navis「船」加 agere「驾驶」构成；意为掌舵行船，而非讨价还价。

entries.definition: The adjective built on the same verb: open to being discussed, or able to be transferred.
entries.definitionCN: 同出于这个动词的形容词：可以商量的，或可以转让的。

entries.definition: The prefixed form: to open the terms of an agreement again and bargain them afresh.
entries.definitionCN: 加前缀的形式：重新打开已达成的条件再谈一遍。

entries.definition: To argue over price or terms in a market; it is the everyday, usually smaller-scale word.
entries.definitionCN: 在市场上为价格或条件争来讲去；是日常、通常规模较小的说法。

entries.definition: To stand between two sides and help them agree; the mediator may not be a party to the deal.
entries.definitionCN: 站在两方之间帮助他们达成一致；调停者本身可能并非交易的一方。

entries.definition: To arrange a deal between others, often for a fee; the broker acts on behalf of the parties.
entries.definitionCN: 为他人安排交易，常收取费用；经纪人代表当事人行事。

entries.definition: To bring a dispute to an end and fix the terms; it names the closing moment rather than the talking.
entries.definitionCN: 把争端结束并定下条件；命名的是收尾那一刻，而不是商谈过程。

normalIntro.en: Normal associations: real morphemes, real fixed phrases and real word relatives, not invented rhymes.
normalIntro.cn: 正常联想：真实的构词成分、真实搭配与真实同族词，而非编造的顺口溜。

normal.en: Neg- 'not' plus otium 'leisure': business is literally the opposite of free time.
normal.cn: neg-「不」加 otium「闲暇」：生意字面上就是「没有闲功夫」。

normal.en: The family runs negotiate, negotiation, negotiator, negotiable, renegotiate.
normal.cn: 同族词包括 negotiate、negotiation、negotiator、negotiable、renegotiate。

normal.en: Fixed phrases pair it with contracts and prices: negotiate a contract, negotiate a price.
normal.cn: 固定搭配把它与合同、价格配在一起：协商合同、商议价格。

normal.en: The same verb crosses obstacles: negotiate a bend, negotiate the narrow ledge.
normal.cn: 同一个动词也用于越过障碍：通过弯道、走过窄石檐。

normal.en: Banks negotiate drafts, so the word appears in finance as well as diplomacy.
normal.cn: 银行会兑付汇票，因此这个词既在外交也在金融里出现。

abstract.en: Picture two people carrying one table through a narrow door, each tilting his own end.
abstract.cn: 想象两个人抬一张桌子过窄门，各抬自己那一头并各自倾斜。

abstract.en: Picture a rope pulled from both banks until it is taut but not broken.
abstract.cn: 想象一条绳从两岸同时收紧，绷直却没有断。

abstract.en: Picture a path that exists only where two sets of footprints overlap.
abstract.cn: 想象一条只存在于两串脚印重合处的路。

examples.en: The two governments negotiated for months before signing anything.
examples.cn: 两国政府在签字之前谈了好几个月。

examples.en: He negotiated a lower rent by offering to repair the roof himself.
examples.cn: 他提出自己修屋顶，以此谈低了房租。

examples.en: The old road negotiates the cliff in a series of tight turns.
examples.cn: 那条老路用一连串急弯绕过悬崖。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「ne（不）+ goti（闲）+ ate」——不得闲，就得去谈生意 → 谈判

root: 拉丁 negotiari「经商」出自 negotium「事务、生意」= neg-（不）+ otium（闲暇）；「谈成协议」义为后世收窄而来。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses start from business as the opposite of leisure: people talk terms, terms harden into a deal, and the same knack of getting through is then applied to obstacles, ground, storm and paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项从「生意即不得闲」出发：人们先谈条件，条件凝成交易，随后同一套「过得去」的本事被用于障碍、地形、风暴与票据。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two boats in a narrow channel each give half a rudder and both pass through.
core.cn: 核心意象：两艘船在窄水道里各让半舵，双方都过去了。

branches.en: TALKING INTO TERMS: proposals move between the parties until a deal exists.
branches.cn: 谈出条款：方案在双方之间来回，直到交易成形。

branches.en: CONTROLLED PASSAGE: a bill or an aircraft is brought through a hard stretch without damage.
branches.cn: 稳妥通过：法案或飞机被稳稳带过一段难走的路。

branches.en: PHYSICAL AND COMMERCIAL ROOT: crossing ground and trading goods are the two oldest branches.
branches.cn: 路与货：穿越地形与买卖货物，是最老的两支。

branches.en: PAPER PASSED ON: a draft changes hands, and the verb names the passing.
branches.cn: 票据易手：汇票从一只手到另一只手，动词命名的正是这次传递。

branches.en: GAIN EXTRACTED: bargaining is also the art of pulling a concession toward oneself.
branches.cn: 争得好处：谈判也是把让步拉向自己这一边的本事。

intro.en: Negotiate is a Latin verb made of a negative particle and a noun for leisure, which is why the family can be read as a small sentence about work.
intro.cn: negotiate 是一个由否定小品词与「闲暇」之名词构成的拉丁动词，因此这个词族可以读成一句关于「工作」的小句子。

latinIntro.en: Latin negotium yields negotiari, negotiator and negotiatio, and those in turn give the English family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁 negotium 衍生 negotiari、negotiator 与 negotiatio，这些又衍生出英语的整个词族。

items.example: The particle turns leisure into its absence.
items.exampleCN: 这个小品词把「闲暇」变成「不得闲」。

items.example: The noun supplies the second half of the compound.
items.exampleCN: 这个名词提供复合词的后一半。

items.example: The compound began as a description of work.
items.exampleCN: 这个复合词最初是对「工作」的描述。

items.example: The verb entered English through this form.
items.exampleCN: 英语的动词正是经这个形式传入。
他们就合同进行了谈判。

items.meaning: able to be discussed or transferred

items.example: The lease was renegotiated last spring.
items.exampleCN: 租约去年春天重新谈过。

latinEntries.structure: negotiari, negotiatus sum (deponent verb, first conjugation)

definition_zh: 谈判；协商；议价；通过（弯道、障碍）；（票据）兑现
definition_en: the process of discussing something in order to reach an agreement, or the successful passing of a difficult route or a financial instrument
core_image: 两个人隔桌而坐，桌上摊着一张纸，各自把笔移到中间那条线的两侧。
scene: 两家公司在会议室里逐条修改合同，先把价格放一边。They began a long negotiation over delivery dates.
sceneCN: 这里 negotiation 是“为达成协议而进行的谈判”（第 1 个义项）；句意：他们开始就交货日期进行长时间的谈判；对应第 1 个义项。

pos.zh: 谈判；协商；议价；（弯道、障碍的）通过；（票据的）兑现、转让

derivatives.zh: 谈判；协商；通过（险处）；兑现（票据）
谈判者；协商代表
可谈判的；可兑现的
重新谈判；重新协商

senses.title: Talk aimed at agreement
senses.definition: the process of discussion between parties who want an agreement but do not yet share the same terms
senses.definitionCN: 希望达成协议但条件尚未一致的各方向进行讨论的过程
senses.example: The negotiation lasted three days before both sides signed.
senses.exampleCN: 谈判持续了三天，双方才签字。
senses.why: The word names the whole process, not one offer: parties move positions until a text can be accepted by both.
senses.whyCN: 这个词命名的是整个过程，而不是某一次报价：各方不断移动立场，直到出现双方都能接受的文本。

senses.title: Bargaining over price and terms
senses.titleCN: 议价磋商：一项一项地换条件
senses.definition: bargaining in which price, quantity, delivery, or other terms are traded against each other
senses.definitionCN: 就价格、数量、交货或其他条款相互交换让步的讨价还价
senses.example: The price was settled in a separate negotiation over volume discounts.
senses.exampleCN: 价格在另一场关于批量折扣的议价中确定。
senses.why: Commerce turns agreement into a trade of terms: one side gives on price, the other gives on time, and the sum must still balance.
senses.whyCN: 商业把协议变成条款交换：一方在价格上让步，另一方在时间上让步，总和仍须平衡。

senses.title: Diplomatic bargaining
senses.titleCN: 外交谈判：国家之间的文字较量
senses.definition: formal talks between states or political groups, often over conflict, borders, or treaties
senses.definitionCN: 国家或政治集团之间就冲突、边界或条约进行的正式会谈
senses.example: The peace negotiation produced a ceasefire but no final border.
senses.exampleCN: 和平谈判带来了停火，却没有确定最终边界。
senses.why: When the parties are states, the same process carries public authority: what is agreed becomes a document that binds populations, not just signers.
senses.whyCN: 当各方是国家时，同一过程带有公共权威：谈成的内容会成为约束民众而不仅是签字者的文件。

senses.title: Dealing over work and pay
senses.titleCN: 合同薪酬谈判：把自己的条件摆上桌
senses.definition: talks between an employer and an employee or union about wages, hours, and working conditions
senses.definitionCN: 雇主与雇员或工会就工资、工时与劳动条件进行的会谈
senses.example: Her salary negotiation gained a raise and an extra week of leave.
senses.exampleCN: 她的薪酬谈判争取到了加薪和额外一周假期。
senses.why: Here the abstract process becomes personal: the terms being traded are the conditions of one's daily life, so preparation and timing matter.
senses.whyCN: 这里抽象过程变得切身：被交换的条款是一个人日常生活的条件，因此准备与时机都很重要。

senses.title: Getting a vehicle round a bend
senses.titleCN: 过弯：把车身稳稳带过弯道
senses.definition: the act of steering or driving a vehicle safely through a curve or narrow passage
senses.definitionCN: 操纵车辆安全通过弯道或狭窄路段的行为
senses.example: The bus slowed for the sharp negotiation of the mountain road.
senses.exampleCN: 大巴减速以通过山路的急弯。
senses.why: From 'dealing with a difficulty' comes the physical sense: the driver negotiates the curve as a rider negotiates a rough path.
senses.whyCN: 从“应对困难”引申出物理义：司机把车稳稳带过弯道，就像骑手带马穿过一段崎岖小路。

senses.title: Passing an obstacle
senses.titleCN: 越过险处：从障碍中穿过去
senses.definition: the successful passing of a physical obstruction, such as a fence, a reef, or rough ground
senses.definitionCN: 成功穿过栅栏、暗礁或崎岖地面等物理障碍
senses.example: The boat's negotiation of the reef took all the crew's attention.
senses.exampleCN: 船只穿越暗礁的过程让全体船员全神贯注。
senses.why: The sense keeps the core idea of dealing with something difficult, but the difficulty is now ground or water rather than another person.
senses.whyCN: 这一义项保留“应对难事”的核心意思，但难事从“另一个人”变成了地面或水面。

senses.title: Cashing or transferring an instrument
senses.titleCN: 票据兑现：让一张纸变成钱
senses.definition: the passing of a cheque, bill, or other financial instrument through the banking system so that it is paid or transferred
senses.definitionCN: 让支票、汇票等金融票据经银行系统完成付款或转让
senses.example: The negotiation of the cheque failed because the signature did not match.
senses.exampleCN: 这张支票因签名不符而未能兑现。
senses.why: A financial instrument must also be 'carried through' a system; the old commercial sense of negotiation survives in banking as the successful passage of paper.
senses.whyCN: 金融票据也必须“穿过”一套系统；negotiation 古老的商业义项在银行领域以“票据顺利通过”的形式留存下来。

senses.title: Agreeing on what words mean
senses.titleCN: 意义协商：边说边确认对方懂了
senses.definition: the interactive process by which speakers adjust wording until both understand a meaning in the same way
senses.definitionCN: 说话者调整措辞，直到双方以相同方式理解某一含义的互动过程
senses.example: In the language class, the negotiation of meaning happened through gestures and repetition.
senses.exampleCN: 在语言课上，意义协商通过手势和重复完成。
senses.why: Even without a contract, two minds must reach a shared version of what a word refers to; that temporary agreement is a negotiation too.
senses.whyCN: 即使没有合同，两个头脑也必须就一个词指什么达成共同版本；这种临时一致同样是一场谈判。

intro.en: Negotiation comes from Latin negotiatio, business or trade, from negotiari, to do business, and negotium, a matter of business. Its literal makeup is 'not leisure'.
intro.cn: negotiation 来自拉丁语 negotiatio“生意、交易”，出自动词 negotiari“做买卖”与名词 negotium“事务、业务”。其字面构成是“不闲暇”。

items.en: Otium meant leisure, ease, or time free from public affairs. It is the peaceful half of the word's ancestry.
items.cn: otium 意为闲暇、安逸，或免于公共事务的时间；它是这个词祖先中安静的那一半。

items.en: Negotium joined nec- 'not' to otium: not-leisure, hence business, employment, and a matter requiring effort.
items.cn: negotium 把 nec-“不”与 otium 结合：不闲暇，因而指业务、职务，以及需要费力的事务。

items.en: The verb meant to carry on business, to trade, and also to transact or manage a matter.
items.cn: 该动词意为做买卖、从事交易，也指经办或处理一桩事务。

items.en: The noun named business, traffic in goods, and the conduct of a transaction. It did not yet mean formal talks.
items.cn: 该名词指生意、货物交易以及交易的处理，当时还没有“正式会谈”的意思。

items.en: French narrowed the word toward the talks that precede a transaction, and English borrowed that sense in the 16th century.
items.cn: 法语把词义收窄到交易之前的商谈，英语在 16 世纪借入了这一含义。

items.en: Diplomacy, labour relations, and banking each kept a branch: talks, bargaining, and the passing of an instrument through a system.
items.cn: 外交、劳资关系与银行各自保留了一条分支：会谈、议价，以及票据在系统中的通过。

note.en: The first group is the negotiate family; the second compares ways of settling a difference, from friendly talk to third-party decision.
note.cn: 第一组是 negotiate 词族；第二组比较解决分歧的方式，从友好商谈到第三方裁决。

entries.definition: to discuss in order to agree, or to get past a difficulty. It names the action.
entries.definitionCN: 为达成一致而商谈，或越过困难；命名的是动作。

entries.definition: a person who takes part in talks on behalf of a side. It names the actor, not the process.
entries.definitionCN: 代表一方参加谈判的人；命名的是行动者，不是过程。

entries.definition: open to being changed by agreement, or able to be transferred as payment. It describes a quality of terms.
entries.definitionCN: 可经协商改变的，或可作为支付转让的；描述条款的性质。

entries.definition: hard trading of offers, especially over price. It sounds more competitive than negotiation.
entries.definitionCN: 围绕报价的强硬交换，尤指价格；比 negotiation 更有竞争味。

entries.definition: help from a neutral third party to reach agreement. The parties still decide, but someone else runs the talk.
entries.definitionCN: 由中立第三方协助达成协议；仍由当事方决定，但谈话由他人主持。

entries.definition: settlement by an outside judge whose decision binds the parties. It replaces negotiation with a ruling.
entries.definitionCN: 由外部裁决者作出有约束力的决定；以裁决取代谈判。

entries.definition: asking for opinions before deciding. It gathers views but does not require agreement.
entries.definitionCN: 决定前征求意见；收集看法，但不要求达成一致。

normalIntro.en: Real parts only: nec- 'not' plus otium 'leisure'. Business is literally not-leisure, and negotiation is the talk that business requires.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分：nec-“不”加 otium“闲暇”。业务字面上就是“不闲暇”，而 negotiation 是业务所需的商谈。

normal.en: Not-leisure: the moment people stop relaxing and start trading terms.
normal.cn: 不闲暇：人们停止放松、开始交换条件的那一刻。

normal.en: A negotiation is a table with two pens and one text between them.
normal.cn: 谈判就是一张桌子、两支笔，以及中间那一份文本。

normal.en: In banking, negotiation is paper passing through a system; in driving, it is a car passing through a curve.
normal.cn: 在银行，negotiation 是票据穿过系统；在驾驶，是车穿过弯道。

normal.en: Salary negotiation trades hours of your life for a number on a contract.
normal.cn: 薪酬谈判用你生命中的小时数换合同上的一个数字。

normal.en: Language learners negotiate meaning with gestures before they find the word.
normal.cn: 语言学习者先用手势协商意义，然后才找到那个词。

abstract.en: Negotiation begins only where two sides are both dependent and unwilling to lose the other.
abstract.cn: 谈判只始于双方既相互依赖、又不愿失去对方的地方。

abstract.en: The word's ancestry says business is the absence of leisure; the modern noun says agreement is the absence of easy silence.
abstract.cn: 这个词的祖先说业务是闲暇的缺席；现代名词则说协议是轻松沉默的缺席。

abstract.en: To negotiate a bend is to accept that the path will not be straight; every agreement has a curve built into it.
abstract.cn: 把车带过一个弯道，就是接受道路不会笔直；每份协议里都内置了一道弯。

examples.en: The union entered negotiations with a single demand: a fixed schedule two weeks in advance.
examples.cn: 工会带着一项诉求进入谈判：提前两周给出固定排班。

examples.en: Years of practice let the old driver negotiate the narrow bridge without slowing much.
examples.cn: 多年练习让老司机几乎不减速就通过了那座窄桥。

examples.en: The cheque failed negotiation because the account had been closed.
examples.cn: 这张支票未能兑现，因为账户已经销户。

dict_mnemonic.text: nego（不）+ tiation（歇）——不歇着，坐下来谈条件，就是谈判。

root: 源自拉丁语 negotiatio（生意、交易），出自 negotium（事务、业务），字面为 nec-“不”+ otium“闲暇”，即“不闲暇之事”；后经法语收窄为“交易前的商谈”，再扩展出外交、劳资、过弯与票据兑现等义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of negotiation. The core is always a difficult passage made manageable: two sides pass from disagreement to agreement, a driver passes a curve, a cheque passes through a bank, or two speakers pass into shared meaning.
sensesIntro.cn: negotiation 的八个义项，核心始终是“让一段难走的路变得可走”：双方从分歧走到一致，司机通过弯道，支票穿过银行系统，两个说话者进入共同理解。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two people at a table, one sheet of paper, and each pen moving toward the middle line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两人隔桌，一张纸，两支笔各自向中间那条线移动。

chain: FRENCH NEGOCIATION TALKS BEFORE A DEAL
ENGLISH NEGOTIATION THE PROCESS OF REACHING TERMS

branches.en: MAKING A DEAL: the general process and the item-by-item trade of price and terms.
branches.cn: 达成交易：一般谈判过程，与逐项交换价格和条款的议价。

branches.en: TALKS WITH WEIGHT: state-to-state diplomacy and employer-to-employee bargaining.
branches.cn: 有分量的会谈：国家对国家的外交，与雇主对雇员的劳资谈判。

branches.en: PHYSICAL PASSAGE: steering through a bend and passing a reef or rough ground.
branches.cn: 物理通过：驾车过弯，以及穿过暗礁或崎岖地面。

branches.en: FINANCIAL PASSAGE: a cheque or bill carried through the banking system.
branches.cn: 金融通过：支票或汇票经银行系统完成流转。

branches.en: SHARED MEANING: speakers adjusting words until both mean the same thing.
branches.cn: 共享意义：说话者调整措辞，直到双方所指相同。

intro.en: Negotiation is negotiate plus -ion, the action-noun suffix. The family adds -or for the person, -able for what can be traded or changed, and re- for doing it again.
intro.cn: negotiation 是 negotiate 加 -ion（动作名词后缀）。词族用 -or 表示人，-able 表示可交易或可更改，re- 表示重新进行。

latinIntro.en: The Latin base is otium, leisure, negated by nec-. Negotium and negotiari are the business words built on that negation.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁词基是 otium“闲暇”，由 nec- 否定。negotium 与 negotiari 就是建立在这一否定之上的业务用语。

items.meaning: leisure, ease, freedom from public business
items.meaningCN: 闲暇；安逸；免于公共事务
items.example: Otium in Roman life meant time for letters and thought.
items.exampleCN: 在罗马生活中，otium 指用于写信与思考的时间。

items.meaning: to discuss for agreement, or to get past a difficulty

definition_zh: 邻居；邻人；邻近的人或物；毗邻
definition_en: a person who lives next door or close by; a person or thing standing beside another; and, as a verb, to be next to a place
core_image: 两家院墙之间只隔一道矮篱，篱上晾着同一根绳子上的衣物
scene: 楼道里的纸箱还没拆完，对门的人先端来一壶热水。The neighbour across the hall brought a kettle of hot water before the boxes were even opened.
sceneCN: 这里 neighbour 是「邻居」（第 1 个义项：住在近旁的人）；句意为纸箱还没打开，对门那位就端来一壶热水。图中可辨识物件：楼道、纸箱、水壶。

senses.title: A person who lives close by
senses.definition: someone who lives next door or very near to one's home
senses.definitionCN: 住在隔壁或离家很近的人
senses.example: Our neighbour upstairs plays the piano every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 楼上那位邻居每天傍晚弹钢琴。
senses.why: The Old English compound joins neah, near, with gebur, a dweller, so the word names the person who dwells near you rather than a friend or a relative.
senses.whyCN: 古英语复合词把 neah（近）与 gebur（居住者）拼在一起，字面上指的就是「住得近的人」，与朋友或亲戚无关。

senses.title: A person or thing placed beside another
senses.definition: the person sitting or standing beside you, or a thing lying next to another of its kind
senses.definitionCN: 坐在或站在你旁边的人，或与其他同类相邻的事物
senses.example: She leaned towards her neighbour at the table to hear the toast.
senses.exampleCN: 她凑向同桌的邻座，想听清祝酒词。
senses.why: Because the word marks only position, it can be used for a stranger in the next seat, and the same logic lets it describe a country lying beside another.
senses.whyCN: 这个词只标记位置，所以能用来指旁边座位上的陌生人，同样的逻辑也让它可以形容一个挨着另一个的国家。

senses.title: To stand next to a place
senses.definition: to be situated immediately beside or near a particular place
senses.definitionCN: 位于某处紧邻的位置
senses.example: The small farm neighbours a protected stretch of river.
senses.exampleCN: 这座小农场毗邻一段受保护的河道。
senses.why: Having named the dweller nearby, English turns the word into a verb for the dwelling itself standing beside another, which is a short step from a person to a place.
senses.whyCN: 既然已经指「住在近旁的人」，英语就把这个词改成动词，指房屋本身紧挨着另一处；从人到地点只差一小步。

intro.en: Neighbour is an Old English compound of two plain words, one meaning near and one meaning dweller. The British spelling keeps ou, and American English writes neighbor.
intro.cn: neighbour 是古英语里两个很朴素的词拼成的，一个表示「近」，一个表示「居住者」。英式拼写保留 ou，美式写作 neighbor。

items.en: The first element goes back to a reconstructed Germanic root for near, the same source as near and the archaic nigh.
items.cn: 第一个成分可上溯到日耳曼语中表示「近」的重构词根，与 near、古旧的 nigh 同源。

items.en: Neah meant near or close, and it survives as the first half of the compound neahgebur.
items.cn: neah 意为近、靠近，作为复合词 neahgebur 的前半保留下来。

items.en: Gebur meant a dweller or a fellow worker of the land, so neahgebur was the person living close by.
items.cn: gebur 指居住者或一同种地的人，所以 neahgebur 就是住得不远的人。

items.en: Middle English reshaped the word as neighebor, and the vowel and spelling shifted several times before settling.
items.cn: 中古英语把它改写成 neighebor，元音和拼写来回变过几次才固定下来。

items.en: Modern British English keeps neighbour with ou, while American English simplifies it to neighbor; the meaning and the history are the same.
items.cn: 现代英式英语保留带 ou 的 neighbour，美式简化为 neighbor；两者的含义与来历完全相同。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the near element or merely the sound; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who live in a place.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「近」这一成分的词，以及只是读音相近的词；近义组收表示住在某处的人。

entries.definition: Close in space or time, the idea that also sits inside the first half of neighbour.
entries.definitionCN: 在空间或时间上接近的；neighbour 的前半也藏着这个「近」的想法。

entries.definition: An older word for near, now mostly literary or dialectal.
entries.definitionCN: 表示「近」的较古老词，现多用于文学或方言。

entries.definition: The long loud cry of a horse; it only looks and sounds like neighbour, and its root is imitative.
entries.definitionCN: 马的长嘶声；只是与 neighbour 形音相近，词源是拟声，二者无关。

entries.definition: A person who lives in a particular place.
entries.definitionCN: 住在某个地方的人；居民。

entries.definition: A person who lives in a particular house or area, often used in compounds.
entries.definitionCN: 住在某处房屋或地区的人，常用于复合词。

entries.definition: A person who lives in the area being talked about.
entries.definitionCN: 住在所谈地区的人；本地人。

normalIntro.en: The word is a compound of near and dweller, and the British spelling keeps an ou that American English drops.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词由「近」与「居住者」复合而成，英式拼写保留一个美式会去掉的 ou。

normal.en: Neah means near and gebur means dweller, so a neighbour is simply the dweller nearest to you.
normal.cn: neah 意为近，gebur 意为居住者，所以邻居就是离你最近的居住者。

normal.en: The -bour part is the old word for a dweller, not the English word for a harbour, so do not read it as a port.
normal.cn: 拼写里的 -bour 是古语「居住者」，不是英语里表示港口的词，别把它读成码头。

normal.en: The verb use follows the noun, since a farm can neighbour a river: the word only marks what stands close.
normal.cn: 动词用法跟着名词走，农场可以 neighbour 一条河，因为这个词只标记「紧挨着」的位置。

normal.en: American English writes neighbor, and the shorter form follows the same pattern as harbor and color.
normal.cn: 美式写作 neighbor，缩短的拼写与 harbor、color 遵循同一规律。

normal.en: Next-door neighbour is the fixed phrase for the person in the house beside yours.
normal.cn: next-door neighbour 是固定说法，指紧挨着你家的那户人。

abstract.en: A word built from near and dweller turns geography into a relationship: closeness itself becomes a kind of company.
abstract.cn: 一个由「近」和「居住者」拼成的词，把地理变成关系：距离近本身就成了一种陪伴。

abstract.en: The British ou and the American missing u are the same word wearing two passports.
abstract.cn: 英式多写一个 u、美式省掉它，是同一个词拿着两本护照。

abstract.en: Calling a country a neighbour borrows the warmth of a doorstep for something as cold as a border.
abstract.cn: 把一个国家叫作 neighbour，是把门槛边的暖意借给了边界这样冰冷的东西。

examples.en: Our neighbour upstairs plays the piano every evening.
examples.cn: 楼上那位邻居每天傍晚弹钢琴。

examples.en: She turned to her neighbour at the table and smiled.
examples.cn: 她转向同桌的邻座，笑了一下。

examples.en: The farm neighbours a stretch of protected river.
examples.cn: 这座农场毗邻一段受保护的河道。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the person who dwells near; from that, the meaning widens to anyone or anything beside you and then becomes a verb.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是「住得不远的人」；由此词义扩到身边任何人或物，最后又变成动词。

latinIntro.en: This word is Germanic in origin and has no reliable Latin cognate; its parts and its family are Old English and English.

definition_zh: 街区；居住区；邻里；附近；大约
definition_en: the area around where someone lives; the people living there; and, in fixed phrases, nearness in place or a rough amount
core_image: 一排低矮的房子围出一个小广场，孩子在三轮车旁追跑
scene: 街角的小店把长桌搬到门外，各家端来自己做的菜。The whole neighbourhood turned out for the street party.
sceneCN: 这里 neighbourhood 是「街坊邻里」（第 2 个义项：住在这一带的人）；句意为整条街的街坊都出来参加街头聚会。图中可辨识物件：长桌、端菜的托盘、街角小店。

derivatives.zh: neighbourhood 的基础词，义为「邻居；毗邻」
由基础词 neighbour 加 -ing 构成，义为「邻近的；相邻的」

senses.title: The area around one's home
senses.definition: the part of a town where someone lives, together with the streets and buildings around their home
senses.definitionCN: 一个人居住的那一片城区，包括住宅周围的街道与建筑
senses.example: She knows every shop in the neighbourhood.
senses.exampleCN: 这一带的每家店铺她都熟。
senses.why: The suffix -hood turns a neighbour into the state or range of neighbours, so the word starts as the zone marked out by people living near one another.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -hood 把 neighbour 变成「邻里所构成的状态或范围」，所以这个词最初就是由相互住得近的人划定的一片地带。

senses.title: The people who live in that area
senses.definition: the residents of such an area considered together as a community
senses.definitionCN: 把这一带的居民作为一个共同体来看
senses.example: The neighbourhood raised money for the new playground.
senses.exampleCN: 街坊们为建新游乐场凑了钱。
senses.why: Since the zone is named after the people inside it, the same word slides from the place to the people, a habit English often shows with words of community.
senses.whyCN: 既然这片地带是因住在里面的人而得名，同一个词就从地点滑到人身上，这是英语里表示共同体的词常见的走向。

senses.title: Nearness in place
senses.definition: the state of being close to a particular place, used in the fixed phrase in the neighbourhood of
senses.definitionCN: 靠近某一地点的状态，用于固定说法「在……附近」
senses.example: They bought a flat in the neighbourhood of the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站附近买了一套公寓。
senses.why: A neighbourhood is space around a point, so the word can serve in a purely spatial phrase that names no residents at all.
senses.whyCN: 街区本身就是某一点周围的空间，所以这个词能用在纯讲位置的短语里，完全不提住在那里的人。

senses.title: A rough amount or range
senses.definition: an approximate figure or amount, used in the phrase in the neighbourhood of
senses.definitionCN: 大致的数字或数量，用于短语「大约、上下」
senses.example: The repair will cost in the neighbourhood of three hundred pounds.
senses.exampleCN: 这次修理大约要花三百英镑。
senses.why: Approximation is spatial nearness moved onto numbers: a figure close to the target is treated as the value living nearby.
senses.whyCN: 近似就是把空间上的「靠近」挪到数字上：接近目标的数字，被当成住在旁边的那个值。

intro.en: Neighbourhood is neighbour plus the old suffix -hood, the same ending that builds childhood and brotherhood.
intro.cn: neighbourhood 是 neighbour 加上古老的词尾 -hood，与 childhood、brotherhood 用的是同一个词尾。

items.en: The suffix had meant condition, state or rank, and it became -hood in modern English.
items.cn: 词尾 hād 意为状况、状态或身份，在现代英语里变成 -hood。

items.en: The base word named the person who dwells near, as a compound of near and dweller.
items.cn: 基础词由「近」与「居住者」复合，指住得不远的人。

items.en: Middle English formed neighbourhood for the state of being neighbours and for the district where they lived.
items.cn: 中古英语构成 neighbourhood，既指互为邻居的关系，也指他们居住的地段。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the word is common for a district of a town and for the people in it.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，这个词已常用来指城里的一片地段以及住在里面的人。

items.en: Modern British English keeps neighbourhood and American English writes neighborhood, while the fixed phrase in the neighbourhood of extends the word to nearness and rough amounts.
items.cn: 现代英式保留 neighbourhood，美式写作 neighborhood；固定短语 in the neighbourhood of 又把词义扩到「附近」和「大约」。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words built with the same -hood suffix; the near-meaning group gathers words for districts and their people.
note.cn: 形近组收用同一个 -hood 词尾构成的词；近义组收表示地段及其居民的词。

entries.definition: The period of life when a person is a child.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人身为孩子的时期；童年。

entries.definition: The relationship between brothers, or a group united by a shared cause.
entries.definitionCN: 兄弟之间的关系，或为共同事业联合起来的团体。

entries.definition: The state of being untrue, or a statement that is untrue.
entries.definitionCN: 虚假的状态，或一句不实的话。

entries.definition: A defined part of a town or country.
entries.definitionCN: 城镇或国家中划定的区域。

entries.definitionCN: 某一地点附近的区域。

entries.definition: The people of a particular area considered together.
entries.definitionCN: 把某一地区的人作为一个整体来看的群体。

normalIntro.en: The word is neighbour plus -hood, and the suffix does the same work it does in childhood: it turns a person into a state or a stretch of life.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 neighbour 加 -hood，词尾的作用与在 childhood 里一样：把人变成一种状态或一段生活。

normal.en: The suffix -hood comes from an Old English word for condition, so neighbourhood is the condition or zone of being neighbours.
normal.cn: -hood 出自古英语中表示「状况」的词，所以 neighbourhood 就是「互为邻居」的状况或范围。

normal.en: Childhood, brotherhood and neighbourhood all use the same ending, which is why they look and feel alike.
normal.cn: childhood、brotherhood、neighbourhood 用的是同一个词尾，所以它们看上去、读起来都很像。

normal.en: American English writes neighborhood, dropping the u that British English keeps.
normal.cn: 美式写作 neighborhood，去掉了英式保留的 u。

normal.en: The phrase 「in the neighbourhood of」 works for both a place and a number, so it means near as well as about.
normal.cn: 短语「in the neighbourhood of」既能接地点又能接数字，所以既表示「附近」也表示「大约」。

normal.en: Neighbourhood watch is a real arrangement in which residents keep an eye on one another's homes.
normal.cn: neighbourhood watch 是真实存在的做法，居民互相照看彼此的房子。

abstract.en: Adding -hood to a person makes a place, a quiet reminder that streets are made of the people standing on them.
abstract.cn: 给一个人加上 -hood 就得到一个地方，这悄悄提醒人：街道是由站在上面的人组成的。

abstract.en: One word can mean a district, its residents and an approximate sum, because all three are measured from the same centre.
abstract.cn: 同一个词能指一片地段、住在里面的人以及一个大致的数目，因为三者都从同一个中心量起。

abstract.en: A word that turns nearness into a number shows how easily English moves from space to quantity.
abstract.cn: 一个把「靠近」变成数字的词，说明英语从空间滑到数量有多容易。

examples.en: The whole neighbourhood came out for the street party.
examples.cn: 整条街的街坊都出来参加街头聚会。

examples.en: She has lived in this neighbourhood for thirty years.
examples.cn: 她在这个街区住了三十年。

examples.en: The cost will be in the neighbourhood of two hundred pounds.

senses.title: Not one and not the other of two
senses.definition: not either of two people or things that have just been mentioned
senses.definitionCN: 刚刚提到的两个人或两样东西，一个也不是
senses.example: Neither of the two answers is correct.
senses.exampleCN: 两个答案都不对。
senses.why: The word is a contraction of the Old English phrase for not which of the two, so its whole job is to sweep both options away in a single gesture.
senses.whyCN: 这个词是古英语中「两者中的哪一个都不是」这一说法的缩合，所以它全部的活儿就是用一次动作把两个选项一起扫掉。

senses.title: Paired with nor to deny both
senses.definition: used with nor to connect two things that are both denied
senses.definitionCN: 与 nor 连用，连接两样都被否定的事物
senses.example: Neither the driver nor the passengers were hurt.
senses.exampleCN: 司机和乘客都没有受伤。
senses.why: Since the first half already denies both members of a pair, English repeats the denial with nor so that each item is explicitly ruled out.
senses.whyCN: 词的前半已经把一对中的两个都否定了，英语再用 nor 重复一次否定，让每一项都被明确排除。

senses.title: Also not, in agreement with a negative
senses.definition: used after a negative statement to say that the same is true of another person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在否定句之后，表示另一个人或事物情况相同
senses.example: I cannot swim, and neither can my brother.
senses.exampleCN: 我不会游泳，我弟弟也不会。
senses.why: The denying force of the pronoun is reused as a short adverb, so a whole negative clause is compressed into one word plus a reversed subject and verb.
senses.whyCN: 代词里的否定力量被挪作简短副词，于是一整个否定从句被压缩成一个词加倒装的主语和动词。

intro.en: Neither is an Old English contraction of a phrase meaning not either, built from a negative word and the word for which of two.
intro.cn: neither 是古英语里「不是两者中的任何一个」这一说法的缩合，由一个否定词和表示「两者中哪一个」的词合成。

items.en: Na was the plain negative word, meaning no or not, and it supplied the first half of the compound.
items.cn: nā 是普通的否定词，意为「不、没有」，构成复合词的前半。

items.en: Hwaether meant which of the two, and it is the same word that became whether in modern English.
items.cn: hwæþer 意为「两者中的哪一个」，就是现代英语 whether 的来源。

items.en: Nahwther meant not either of the two, and in speech it was shortened to forms such as neither.
items.cn: nāhwæþer 意为「两者中哪一个都不是」，在口语中缩短成 neither 这类形式。

items.en: Middle English settled on spellings like neither, and the word worked both as a pronoun and as a conjunction.
items.cn: 中古英语固定为 neither 这类写法，这个词同时作代词和连词。

items.en: Modern English keeps it as the pronoun, in the paired construction with nor, and in the adverb use of short negative replies.
items.cn: 现代英语保留它作代词、作与 nor 搭配的配对结构，以及简短否定回答里的副词用法。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words sharing the old element for which of two or merely the spelling; the near-meaning group gathers words of outright denial.
note.cn: 形近组收共享「两者中哪一个」这一古老成分的词，以及只是拼写相近的词；近义组收表示彻底否定的词。

entries.definition: One or the other of two, the positive partner of this pair of words.

entries.definition: Lower or underneath, as in the old phrase the nether world; it only looks like neither, and the root is different.
entries.definitionCN: 下面的、下方的，如旧说法「下界」；只是与 neither 拼写相近，词根不同。

entries.definition: Neither masculine nor feminine in grammar; the Latin word means neither, but it is not the English source.
entries.definitionCN: 语法上既非阳性也非阴性；拉丁语原词意为「两者都不」，但它不是英语这个词的来源。

entries.definition: Not one of any number, used for more than two as well as for two.
entries.definitionCN: 任何数量中一个也没有，既可用于两个，也可用于更多。

entries.definition: And not, used to continue a negative statement.
entries.definitionCN: 也不，用于延续一个否定说法。

entries.definition: No person at all, used of people rather than of things.
entries.definitionCN: 一个人也没有，用于人而不用于物。

normalIntro.en: The word is a contraction of not plus which of two, and that double denial is what every one of its uses carries.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是「不」加上「两者中哪一个」的缩合，它每一种用法都带着这层双重否定。

normal.en: The first half is an old negative word, so neither always denies before it chooses.
normal.cn: 前半是一个古老的否定词，所以 neither 总是先否定，再谈选择。

normal.en: The second half is the same element that gives English whether, so the word is literally not whether of the two.
normal.cn: 后半就是给英语 whether 的那个成分，所以这个词字面是「两者中的哪一个都不」。

normal.en: Neither is followed by a singular verb in careful writing, because it denies each member separately.
normal.cn: 在严谨的写作里 neither 后接单数动词，因为它对每一个成员分别加以否定。

normal.en: The paired pattern needs nor, not or, since the second item is denied as well.
normal.cn: 配对结构要用 nor 而不是 or，因为第二项同样被否定。

normal.en: In short replies the word brings inversion, as in neither do I, which copies the order of a question.
normal.cn: 在简短回答里它会带来倒装，如 neither do I，照搬了疑问句的词序。

abstract.en: A word made of not plus which of two shows that a choice can be refused before it is even offered.
abstract.cn: 一个由「不」加「两者中哪一个」构成的词说明：选择可以在被提出之前就被拒绝。

abstract.en: Neither is the grammar of a closed door: two ways stand open, and both are declared shut.
abstract.cn: neither 是一扇关上的门的语法：两条路摆在面前，两条都被宣布关闭。

abstract.en: Its three jobs as pronoun, conjunction and adverb show how one small denial can hold a whole clause together.
abstract.cn: 它兼作代词、连词和副词，说明一个小小的否定能撑起整个从句。

examples.en: Neither of the two cups had been touched.
examples.cn: 两只杯子都没有被动过。

examples.en: I cannot swim, and neither can my brother.
examples.cn: 我不会游泳，我弟弟也不会。

sensesIntro.en: The core sense is the denial of both members of a pair; it divides into the pronoun, the paired conjunction with nor and the adverb of agreement.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心义是把一对中的两个一起否定；由此分出代词、与 nor 搭配的连词，以及表示「也不」的副词。
